create.name: Henry Shukman
create.bio:
Henry Shukman is an English-born Zen teacher, poet and author, appointed a teacher in the Sanbo Zen lineage in 2010 by Yamada Roshi, its international abbot. Raised in Oxford, he came to meditation through a love of Chinese Zen poetry, and after a sudden awakening at nineteen he trained for many years with Roshis John Gaynor, Joan Rieck and Ruben Habito as well as Yamada Roshi. Shinzen Young has also authorised him to teach mindfulness. For years he guided the Mountain Cloud Zen Center, a Santa Fe sangha, and he now holds the title of spiritual director emeritus there.

Before teaching he worked as a full-time writer, publishing prize-winning poetry and fiction, and his poems and essays have appeared in the New Yorker, the Guardian and the New York Times. In One Blade of Grass he wrote about his years of Zen training, while Original Love lays out his teaching as a journey through four 'inns' of practice, from mindfulness and support to absorption and finally awakening. With his nephew Jack he co-founded The Way, a meditation app that leads students along a single graded path of daily sessions he guides himself, and he teaches live online courses and retreats through it. He has taught at Esalen, Google and Harvard Business School.
